verses.text: Josiah was eight years old when he became king and ruled thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes and followed the ways of his ancestor David without turning to the right or left.

In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, he began to seek the God of his ancestor David. In his twelfth year he began clearing Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherah poles, and the carved and cast idols.

They tore down the altars of the Baals in front of him. He cut down the incense altars above them and smashed the Asherah poles and the carved and cast idols. He ground them to dust and scattered it on the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
He burned the bones of the priests on their own altars. In this way he cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
He did the same in the towns and surrounding ruins of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as Naphtali.
He tore down altars, crushed Asherah poles and carved images to powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout Israel. Then he went back to Jerusalem.

In the eighteenth year of his reign, after cleansing the land and the temple, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the city governor, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder to repair the house of the LORD his God.

They went to Hilkiah the high priest and handed over the money brought into God's house. The Levite gatekeepers had collected it from Manasseh, Ephraim, the rest of Israel, all Judah and Benjamin, and the people of Jerusalem.
They handed it to the men overseeing work on the LORD's house, who paid the workers to restore and repair it.
The money went to carpenters and builders to buy cut stone and timber for braces and beams in the buildings the kings of Judah had let fall into ruin.

The men worked faithfully. Jahath and Obadiah, Levites from Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, from Kohath, supervised and directed them, along with other Levites skilled in playing musical instruments.
They oversaw the men who carried loads and directed workers in all kinds of jobs. Some Levites served as scribes, officials, and gatekeepers.
As they brought out the money that had been taken into the LORD's house, Hilkiah the priest found the Book of the LORD's Law given through Moses.
Hilkiah told Shaphan the secretary, "I've found the Book of the Law in the LORD's house." He handed the book to Shaphan.
Shaphan took the book to the king and reported, "Your servants are doing everything you assigned them.
They've taken out the money found in the LORD's house and handed it to the supervisors and workers."
Shaphan the secretary added, "Hilkiah the priest gave me a book." Then he read from it to the king.
When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
He gave orders to Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the secretary, and Asaiah the king's servant.

"Go and ask the LORD for me and for those who remain in Israel and Judah about the words in this book. The LORD has poured out great anger on us because our ancestors failed to obey his word and do everything written here."

Hilkiah and the men the king sent went to Huldah the prophet, who lived in Jerusalem's Second Quarter. She was the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, the keeper of the wardrobe. They told her why they had come.
She said to them, "The LORD, the God of Israel, says to tell the man who sent you to me:
'The LORD says: I'm bringing disaster on this place and its people, all the curses written in the book that was read to the king of Judah.
They abandoned me and burned incense to other gods, provoking my anger with everything they made and did. So my anger will be poured out on this place, and nothing will put it out.'
But tell the king of Judah who sent you to ask the LORD, 'The LORD, the God of Israel, says this about the words you heard:
Your heart was tender. When you heard God's words against this place and its people, you humbled yourself before me, tore your clothes, and wept before me. I have heard you, says the LORD.
I'll gather you to your ancestors. You'll go to your grave in peace, and you won't see the disaster I bring on this place and its people.'" They took this message back to the king.
Then the king summoned all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

He went up to the LORD's house with the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, the priests and Levites, and everyone from the least to the greatest. He read aloud every word of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the LORD's house.

The king stood in his place and made a covenant before the LORD to follow him and keep his commands, testimonies, and statutes with all his heart and soul, carrying out the words of the covenant written in the book.
He had everyone in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand in support. The people of Jerusalem followed the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.

Josiah removed every detestable idol from the lands belonging to the Israelites and had everyone in Israel serve the LORD their God. Throughout his life they continued to follow the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
